title: Decoder Watchdog: constrained-decoder chaos harness & schema metering
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an engineering-level test harness (Decoder Watchdog) that simulates partial/garbled streaming outputs, interleaved tool/function calls, and constrained-decoder failure modes to validate our JSON mode enforcement and schema adherence across models and runtimes.

Scope:
- A reproducible simulator that can inject: truncated token sequences, mid-stream token noise, toolcall markers inserted out-of-band, and KV-cache evictions to surface decoder divergence.
- A schema-metering layer that scores each output on: syntactic JSON validity, schema field coverage, type adherence, and ambiguity heuristics (fields present but null/untyped).
- Canary tests to compare behavior between: (a) stock decoding, (b) constrained-decoder enforcement, and (c) deterministic backoff + structured-repair heuristics.

Why now: Recent regressions in streaming schema compliance (partial emissions during tool calls) have caused degraded downstream parsing and higher error rates in Console rollups. This harness will let us quantify regressions, evaluate fallback strategies, and gate rollout for runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: Decoder Watchdog can orchestrate 10k synthetic streaming sessions with configurable error injection profiles
Schema-meter returns per-session score and per-field failure reasons (missing, wrong-type, truncated)
Baseline vs constrained-decoder A/B produces measurable delta: target >= 90% reduction in parse failures for deterministic toolcall scenarios
Runbook entries generated for top 5 failure modes with owner and mitigation steps
Hook added to canary pipeline to fail releases when schema-meter regression > 5% vs baseline
test_plan: Generate workload mixes: chat-only (60%), single-tool-call (25%), multi-tool-interleave (15%)
Inject fault matrix: {token-drop, duplicate-token, tool-marker-misplaced, early-EOF, kv-eviction}
Compare three decoder strategies across models: open-llama-72B-quant, rdx-13B, rdx-3B-quant
Measure latency impact of constrained-decoder enforcement at p50/p95 and end-to-end parse success rate
Run overnight stress job (12h) to collect stability telemetry and seed flaky-case corpus

2026-03-09 — Dev meeting: Decided to prioritize syntactic repair heuristics (closing braces insertion) as first-line fallback; defer neural-rewrite attempts to later cycle.
2026-03-12 — PR feedback (runtime#3421): Request to expose per-token gating telemetry for downstream routing decisions. Liam to update PR.

2026-03-14 — Liam O'Connor: Implemented schema-meter proto and hooked into canary dashboard; initial run shows constrained-decoder reduces parse errors from 18% -> 4% on synthetic tool-interleave workload.
rollout_notes: Start with internal canary traffic (10% of test tenants) for runtime-1.20. If schema-meter shows regression <= 2% and p95 latency cost < 10ms, expand to 50% for 48h then full rollout. Maintain ability to toggle constrained-decoder per-model via feature flag.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for schema-meter scoring logic
End-to-end simulated session tests with deterministic seeds
Integration test that asserts canary pipeline blocks on regression > threshold
Load test at expected production concurrency to validate latency overhead
Manual review of top 50 failing sessions to validate actionable runbook correctness
